title: Book 1 — Clio, Chapter 27
paragraphs: When the Hellenes of Asia had been conquered and forced to pay tribute, he intended next to build ships and attack those who lived on the islands. All was ready for shipbuilding when — so they say — Bias of Priene (or, according to another version, Pittacus of Mytilene) came to Sardis. Asked by Croesus whether there was any news from Hellas, he stopped the shipbuilding with this reply. “O king,” he said, “the men of the islands are hiring a force of ten thousand horsemen, and with them they mean to march on Sardis and fight against you.” Croesus, supposing the report to be true, said, “May the gods put it into the minds of the islanders to come on horseback against the sons of the Lydians!” The other answered, “O king, I see that you greatly desire to catch the men of the islands riding on horses on the mainland, and there is nothing unreasonable in that wish. But what do you think the islanders have been wishing and praying for ever since they heard that you were going to build ships against them, except to catch the Lydians at sea, so that they might take vengeance on you for the Hellenes on the mainland, whom you hold enslaved?” Croesus, they say, was greatly pleased with this reply, and, thinking the man had spoken well, he obeyed his suggestion and put a stop to the shipbuilding; and on that basis he formed a friendship with the Ionians who lived on the islands.
